name: qdrant_health_check
description:
Confirm the configured Qdrant instance is reachable and responding.

Never raises to the caller: a health check that raises on the exact condition it exists to detect defeats its own purpose. Connection failures are logged and reported in the result's ok/error fields instead, so a client renders them without a tool-call error round-trip.

name: qdrant_collection_create
description:
Create a collection: a single unnamed vector (`vector_size` + `distance`), one or more named vectors (`vectors`, each a full `VectorParams` — size, distance, and optionally its own `multivector_config` for ColBERT-style multi-vectors or `quantization_config`), or a text collection (`text_model`) — exactly one of the three. `sparse_vectors` defines sparse (keyword-style) vectors at creation time.

Text: `text_model` (a fastembed model, e.g. `sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, 384 dims, multilingual, downloaded on first use) creates a `dense` Cosine vector of the model's size and records the model in the collection's metadata, so `text` in `qdrant_points_upsert` and `query_text` in `qdrant_query` embed with it. `text_language` (e.g. "spanish") adds a BM25 index on `text_field` (default `text`) for `bm25_query`: stemmed, accent-folded, stopwords removed where Qdrant has a list for the language (all but armenian and tamil); given alone, it makes a keyword-only collection with no vectors. The embedded local mode (QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH) can't rank such an index — BM25 there needs the default tokenization. `quantization_config` (scalar/product/binary) and `strict_mode_config` apply to the whole collection.

`hnsw_config` and `optimizers_config` set the index and optimizer parameters from the start (they can also be changed later with `qdrant_collection_update`); `on_disk_payload=true` keeps payloads on disk instead of in RAM, which can only be chosen here.

Fails with a clear error if a collection with this name already exists.

Example (simple): {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_size": 4, "distance": "Cosine"} Example (hybrid): {"collection_name": "docs", "vectors": { "dense": {"size": 4, "distance": "Cosine"} }, "sparse_vectors": {"sparse": {}}} Example (multitenant index, payload on disk): {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_size": 4, "hnsw_config": {"m": 0, "payload_m": 16}, "on_disk_payload": true} Example (text, semantic + BM25): {"collection_name": "notes", "text_model": "sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2", "text_language": "spanish"}

name: qdrant_collection_list
description:
List every collection name in the configured Qdrant instance.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_collection_info
qdrant_collection_update
description:
Update optimizer/HNSW/collection/vector params on an existing collection.

`text_models` declares which fastembed model made each existing dense vector (`{"<vector name>": "<model>"}`, `""` for the unnamed vector), so `query_text` and `text` upserts work on a collection built elsewhere — it must be the model the stored vectors were made with, and its size must match the vector's. `null` removes a declaration (e.g. after deleting that vector). A collection with points won't switch a vector to a different model: remove the declaration first if it was wrong. `text_field` names the payload field holding the text (default `text`). Both are kept in the collection's metadata.

Only the fields you pass are changed; omitted ones keep their current value. `quantization_config="disabled"` turns quantization off. `vectors_config`/`sparse_vectors_config` only **adjust** named vectors that already exist (HNSW/quantization/index tuning) — they cannot add a new one; use `qdrant_collection_vector_create` for that, or this fails with Qdrant's own "Not existing vector name" error. Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "optimizers_config": {"indexing_threshold": 10000}}

name: qdrant_collection_delete
description:
Delete a collection and all its points; a no-op if it doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_collection_exists
description:
Check whether a collection exists, without raising if it doesn't.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_points_upsert
description:
Insert or replace points (id + vector or text + payload) in a collection.

`vector` matches the collection's vector config: a plain list for a single unnamed vector; a list of lists for an unnamed multivector; or a dict keyed by vector name for named vectors, where each value is a dense list, a multivector, or a sparse vector (`{"indices": [...], "values": [...]}`). Give `text` instead of `vector` to have it embedded with every model the collection declares (see `qdrant_collection_create`'s `text_model`) and stored in its text field — one text is one point, nothing is split. A text longer than the model reads (128 tokens, ~500 characters, for the multilingual MiniLM) is refused rather than silently cut: split it into several points. Needs the `embeddings` extra.

`update_mode` makes the write conditional: `insert_only` never overwrites an existing id, `update_only` never creates a new one (default `upsert` does both). `update_filter` only overwrites existing points whose current payload matches the filter; ids that don't exist yet are inserted regardless (verified). `wait=false` returns before the write is applied.

Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "payload": {"city": "ny"}} ]} Example (text): {"collection_name": "notes", "points": [ {"id": 1, "text": "Grants for young people's housing", "payload": {"year": 2026}} ]} Example (named dense + sparse): {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": {"dense": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "sparse": {"indices": [1, 7], "values": [0.5, 0.2]}}} ]}

name: qdrant_points_get
qdrant_points_delete
qdrant_points_scroll
description:
Page through all points in a collection, optionally filtered.

Pass the returned `next_page_offset` as `offset` to fetch the next page; `null` means there are no more pages. `limit` is capped per call by the server's QDRANT_MCP_MAX_LIMIT (1000 by default). `with_payload` takes `true`/`false` or a list of keys to return only those.

`order_by` sorts by a payload field instead of by id: a key, or `{"key": ..., "direction": "asc"|"desc", "start_from": value}`; the key needs a payload range index (integer, float or datetime). Paging works differently then: `offset` is rejected, and `next_page_offset` is always `null` even when more points remain — to continue, repeat the call with `start_from` set to the last value you received (points tied on that value are returned again, so de-duplicate by id).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "limit": 50} Example (newest first): {"collection_name": "docs", "limit": 20, "order_by": {"key": "created_at", "direction": "desc"}}

name: qdrant_points_count
description:
Count points in a collection, optionally matching a filter.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_query
description:
Search a collection with Qdrant's unified Query API: vector similarity, hybrid fusion, multi-stage reranking, MMR diversity, payload-based score formulas, ordering by a payload field, or random sampling.

Exactly one query mode is required: - `query_vector` — nearest points to a dense vector, a multivector (list of vectors), a sparse vector (`{"indices": [...], "values": [...]}`), or a point id whose stored vector is reused (that point itself is left out of the results). It must match the vector selected with `using`. Add `mmr` (`diversity` 0..1, `candidates_limit`) to re-order the nearest candidates for diversity: set `candidates_limit` well above `limit` (it defaults to `limit`, which leaves MMR nothing to choose from). `offset` pages through the MMR ranking on Qdrant 1.20 (verified; older servers applied it inside the `limit` re-ranked results, so raise `limit` there instead). - `query_text` — semantic search with plain text: embedded with the model the collection declares for the vector in `using` (`using` can be omitted when it declares exactly one). Needs the `embeddings` extra; `mmr` works as with `query_vector`. - `bm25_query` — keyword search ranked by BM25 (Qdrant 1.20): `using` is a payload field whose `text` index has `scoring` set (defaults to the collection's declared text field). The index's own tokenizer, stemmer and stopwords apply. Needs no embeddings. - `fusion` + 2+ `prefetch` stages — combine retrieval strategies: `"rrf"` (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), `"dbsf"` (Distribution-Based Score Fusion), or `{"method": "rrf", "weights": [2, 1], "k": 60}` for RRF with one weight per stage (a count that doesn't match the stages is rejected by Qdrant). - `formula` — rescore the results of `prefetch` stages (required: a formula without prefetch is rejected). `{"expression": ..., "defaults": {...}}`. An expression is a number; a variable (`"$score"` is the prefetch score, any other string is a payload key); a payload condition (e.g. `{"key": "city", "match": {"value": "sf"}}`, worth 1 if it matches, else 0); or exactly one operator object: `{"sum": [...]}`, `{"mult": [...]}`, `{"neg": e}`, `{"abs": e}`, `{"div": {"left": e, "right": e}}`, `{"sqrt": e}`, `{"pow": {"base": e, "exponent": e}}`, `{"exp": e}`, `{"ln": e}`, `{"log10": e}`, `{"geo_distance": {"origin": {"lat": .., "lon": ..}, "to": "payload.key"}}`, `{"datetime": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`, `{"datetime_key": "payload.key"}`, and the decays `{"exp_decay" | "gauss_decay" | "lin_decay": {"x": e, "target": e, "scale": number, "midpoint": number}}`. A payload key a point lacks needs a value in `defaults`, or Qdrant rejects the query. - `order_by` — sort by a payload field instead of by similarity: a key or `{"key": ..., "direction": "asc"|"desc", "start_from": value}`. The key needs a payload range index (integer, float or datetime). - `sample: "random"` — random points.

A `prefetch` stage is itself a `query_vector`, `query_text` or `bm25_query` query, or a `fusion` of its own nested `prefetch` stages, so pipelines nest: fuse semantic + BM25 in one stage, then rerank. `using` selects a named vector; `lookup_from` resolves `query_vector` from a point id in another collection.

Results: `with_payload` takes `true`/`false` or a list of keys to return only those (e.g. `["title", "url"]`, nested ones as `"meta.author"`) — most of what you read back is payload.

Tuning: `search_params` (`hnsw_ef`, `exact` for brute force, `quantization`: `ignore`/`rescore`/`oversampling`, `indexed_only`, `acorn`), `score_threshold` (drop weaker hits), `limit` + `offset` (paging; `limit` is capped per call by the server's QDRANT_MCP_MAX_LIMIT, 1000 by default — page with `offset` for more), `timeout_seconds` (server-side), and `consistency` (a replica count, or `"majority"`/`"quorum"`/`"all"`; only meaningful on a replicated deployment). Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example (plain): {"collection_name": "docs", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 5} Example (by text): {"collection_name": "docs", "query_text": "housing grants", "limit": 5} Example (semantic + BM25): {"collection_name": "docs", "fusion": "rrf", "prefetch": [ {"query_text": "housing grants", "limit": 20}, {"bm25_query": "housing grants", "limit": 20} ], "limit": 5} Example (hybrid): {"collection_name": "docs", "fusion": "rrf", "prefetch": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "using": "dense", "limit": 20}, {"query_vector": {"indices": [1, 7], "values": [0.5, 0.2]}, "using": "sparse", "limit": 20} ], "limit": 5} Example (diverse results): {"collection_name": "docs", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "mmr": {"diversity": 0.5, "candidates_limit": 50}, "limit": 5} Example (boost one city): {"collection_name": "docs", "prefetch": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 50} ], "formula": {"expression": {"sum": ["$score", {"mult": [0.5, {"key": "city", "match": {"value": "sf"}}]}]}}, "limit": 5} Example (cheapest first): {"collection_name": "docs", "order_by": {"key": "price", "direction": "asc"}, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_query_batch
description:
Run multiple independent queries against one collection in a single round trip — each item takes every query mode and tuning parameter of `qdrant_query` (vector, `query_text`, `bm25_query`, fusion over prefetch, MMR, formula, order_by, sample, search_params, score_threshold, offset); `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "queries": [ {"query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "limit": 5}, {"query_vector": [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5], "limit": 5} ]}

name: qdrant_query_groups
description:
Vector query grouped by a payload field, up to `group_size` hits per group — e.g. the best-matching chunks per source document. Takes every query mode and tuning parameter of `qdrant_query` except `offset` (groups have no paging).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "group_by": "document_id", "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "group_size": 2}

name: qdrant_recommend
qdrant_recommend_batch
description:
Run multiple independent recommend queries against one collection in a single round trip. Each item takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_recommend`; `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "requests": [ {"positive": [1], "negative": [7]}, {"positive": [2, 3]} ]}

name: qdrant_recommend_groups
description:
Recommend query grouped by a payload field, up to `group_size` hits per group. Takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_recommend` except `offset` (groups have no paging).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "group_by": "document_id", "positive": [1, 2], "group_size": 2}

name: qdrant_discover
qdrant_discover_batch
description:
Run multiple independent discover queries against one collection in a single round trip. Each item takes the tuning parameters of `qdrant_discover`; `timeout_seconds` and `consistency` apply to the whole batch.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "requests": [ {"target": 1, "context": [{"positive": 2, "negative": 7}]} ]}

name: qdrant_distance_matrix_pairs
description:
Pairwise distance matrix between a random sample of points: for each of `sample` points, its `limit` closest neighbors among that same sample — returned as a flat list of (a, b, score) pairs.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "sample": 20, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_distance_matrix_offsets
description:
Same distance matrix as `qdrant_distance_matrix_pairs`, in a column-oriented shape (offsets into a shared id list + a parallel score array) — more compact for large samples.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "sample": 20, "limit": 5}

name: qdrant_payload_set
description:
Merge fields into the payload of selected points — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Existing keys not in `payload` are kept. `key` sets a nested sub-field (e.g. `"metadata.author"`) instead of merging at the payload root. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying. A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "payload": {"city": "ny"}}

name: qdrant_payload_overwrite
description:
Replace the entire payload of selected points with `payload` — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Unlike `qdrant_payload_set`, existing keys not in `payload` are dropped. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying. A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "payload": {"city": "ny"}}

name: qdrant_payload_delete
description:
Delete specific payload keys from selected points — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. Other keys are untouched. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying. A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1], "keys": ["city"]}

name: qdrant_payload_clear
description:
Wipe the entire payload of selected points, keeping their vectors — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying. A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "ids": [1]}

name: qdrant_payload_facet
description:
Count distinct values of a payload field across the collection (or a filtered subset) — e.g. how many points per `city`. `exact` trades speed for an exact count instead of an approximation. The field needs a `keyword`, `integer`, `uuid` or `bool` payload index; without one Qdrant answers "No appropriate index for faceting".

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "key": "city", "limit": 20}

name: qdrant_payload_index_create
description:
Create a payload index on `field_name`, speeding up filters that use it. `field_schema` can be a simple type name ("keyword", "integer", "float", "geo", "text", "bool", "datetime", "uuid") or a detailed params object (e.g. a `text` index with a specific tokenizer, or a `keyword` index marked `is_tenant`). If the field already has an index with another schema, it is replaced without warning (verified: integer → keyword drops its range filtering).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "field_name": "city", "field_schema": "keyword"}

name: qdrant_payload_index_delete
description:
Delete the payload index on `field_name`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "field_name": "city"}

name: qdrant_collection_vector_create
qdrant_collection_vector_delete
description:
Remove a named vector (dense or sparse) from a collection — points keep their other vectors and payload. Same server-version requirement as `qdrant_collection_vector_create`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_name": "sparse"}

name: qdrant_points_batch_update
qdrant_vectors_update
description:
Replace the vector(s) of existing points by id — leaves their payload untouched. For a named-vector collection, `vector` is a dict keyed by vector name; for a single unnamed vector, pass a plain vector. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "points": [ {"id": 1, "vector": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]} ]}

name: qdrant_vectors_delete
description:
Remove specific named vectors from selected points, keeping their payload and other vectors — exactly one of `ids`/`points_filter`. An id that doesn't exist fails the whole call ("No point with id … found"), yet the ids that do exist in it are still written (verified) — re-read them before retrying. A filter that matches nothing is not an error.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "vector_names": ["sparse"], "ids": [1]}

name: qdrant_alias_list
qdrant_collection_aliases
description:
List the aliases that point to one collection (an empty list if it has none). Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs_v2"}

name: qdrant_alias_update
description:
Create, rename, re-point or delete aliases — the basis of a zero-downtime reindex: build the new collection, then switch the alias that clients use.

Each operation is exactly one of `create_alias` (`collection_name`, `alias_name`), `rename_alias` (`old_alias_name`, `new_alias_name`) or `delete_alias` (`alias_name`). Operations run in order in one request, all-or-nothing on Qdrant 1.20 (verified: if any operation fails, none is applied, even one whose failure depends on an earlier operation's effect). Older servers (verified on 1.19.0) kept the earlier operations applied — on those, check `qdrant_alias_list` after an error. To switch an alias to another collection, send a single `create_alias`: on an alias name that already exists it re-points it.

Other verified behavior: deleting an alias that doesn't exist is a no-op, not an error; an alias can't take the name of an existing collection (409); creating one for a missing collection fails. Deleting a collection also removes the aliases that pointed to it. No collection data is ever modified.

Example (zero-downtime switch): {"operations": [ {"create_alias": {"collection_name": "docs_v2", "alias_name": "docs"}} ]} Example (rename then delete): {"operations": [ {"rename_alias": {"old_alias_name": "docs", "new_alias_name": "docs_old"}}, {"delete_alias": {"alias_name": "docs_old"}} ]}

name: qdrant_collection_cluster_info
description:
Shard layout of a collection: how many shards it has and, for each local shard, its point count and replica state. Works on a single-node deployment too (one peer, `remote_shards` empty); shard transfers and resharding only ever appear on a distributed deployment. Fails with a clear error if the collection doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_collection_optimizations
qdrant_collection_copy
description:
Copy points (all vectors — dense, sparse and multivector — and payload) from one collection to another of the same Qdrant instance, entirely server-side: the vectors never pass through the model.

The target must already exist with a compatible vector configuration (see `qdrant_collection_info`); this tool does not create it. Use it to re-create a collection with another distance, quantization or HNSW layout, then switch an alias with `qdrant_alias_update`.

Each call copies at most `max_points` points, in batches of `batch_size` (up to 250; lower it for very high-dimensional vectors, since Qdrant rejects a request over 32 MiB), so no single call runs long. If the result has `done: false`, call again with the same arguments and `offset=next_offset`. Points that already exist in the target under the same id are overwritten, so re-running a copy is safe; points that were deleted from the source are not removed from the target. `copy_filter` copies only matching points. Points are visited in id order, so points added to the source with a lower id than the current offset during a long copy are not picked up.

If a batch fails, the error reports how many points were copied and the `offset` to resume from.

Example: {"source_collection": "docs_v1", "target_collection": "docs_v2"} Example (continue): {"source_collection": "docs_v1", "target_collection": "docs_v2", "offset": 1000}

name: qdrant_payload_schema_infer
description:
Profile the payload keys that actually occur in a collection, so filters can be written against real keys instead of guessed ones.

Looks at a random sample of `sample_size` points (optionally limited by `sample_filter`) and reports, per key: the value types seen (`string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `null`), whether it was ever an array, how many sampled points have it (`present_in`), and whether it has a payload index (`indexed`, `index_type`). Keys use the syntax filters expect: `a.b` for nested objects, `a[].b` for objects inside an array. For keys with a keyword/integer/uuid/bool index, `top_values` adds the most frequent values over the **whole collection** (not just the sample), taken from the index; set it to 0 to skip. Also lists indexed keys that no sampled point has (`indexed_but_unseen`).

Because it is a sample, a rare key can be missed: raise `sample_size` (up to 1000) if a field you expect doesn't show up. At most `max_fields` keys are returned, most common first (`fields_truncated` says if more existed).

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_collection_doctor
description:
Diagnose one collection (or alias): read-only checks that each come with the exact tool call that acts on them, so you don't have to know Qdrant's internals.

Rules (`rule` in each finding): - `status`: the collection isn't green — yellow (optimizing), grey (optimizations paused, usually after a restart) or red (an optimization failed; the error is in `evidence`). - `unindexed`: it has points but no vector (HNSW) index yet, so searches scan every point. Collections with sparse vectors are never flagged here. - `memory`: at least 1 GiB of dense vectors held in RAM without quantization (multivectors, on-disk/cold and quantized vectors don't count). - `aliases`: no alias points to it, so a rebuild-and-switch would need a client change. - `text_contract`: only for collections that declare text search (`text_models`): a declared model on a vector that isn't a single dense vector, a text field without a BM25 index, or malformed metadata.

`checked` lists the rules evaluated: always the first four, plus `text_contract` when the collection declares one. A report with no findings means none of these rules fired, not that the collection is optimally configured.

Each finding has a `severity` (error, warning, info), a plain-language `finding`, the numbers it is based on (`evidence`) and, when one exists, a `fix`: a call to another tool of this server, with arguments it accepts as is — except `aliases`, whose alias name is a placeholder to choose. Nothing is applied: calling the fix is up to you.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_search_quality_eval
description:
Measure how much a collection's approximate (HNSW, quantized) search loses against an exact one, and what each configuration costs in latency — so a tuning change is judged by numbers.

Takes `sample` random points the collection already holds and uses each one's vector (the one in `using`; omit it when there's only one) as a query. For each query it runs an exact brute-force search — the ground truth — and an approximate search per `variants` entry (each a `search_params` object such as `{"hnsw_ef": 128}` or `{"quantization": {"rescore": true, "oversampling": 2.0}}`; by default one variant with the collection's own settings). The query point itself is left out of both result lists without a filter (a filter would switch Qdrant to its filtered-search path and measure that instead). Reports, per variant, recall@`limit` (mean and worst query: the share of the exact top-`limit` the approximate search also returned) and latency p50/p95.

Read the numbers with care: points used as their own queries sit inside the data, so recall here is usually higher than for real queries; latency is measured by this server and includes the round trip to Qdrant. Below the indexing threshold there is no HNSW index yet and approximate search is exact, so recall is 1.0 by construction (the report says so). Sparse vectors are always searched exactly and are refused.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "variants": [{}, {"hnsw_ef": 32}, {"hnsw_ef": 256}]}

name: qdrant_snapshot_create
description:
Create a snapshot of one collection's current state.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_list
description:
List the snapshots stored for one collection.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_delete
description:
Delete a collection snapshot, freeing its disk space on the server — does not touch the live collection. Fails if the snapshot doesn't exist.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "snapshot_name": "docs-....snapshot"}

name: qdrant_snapshot_recover
qdrant_snapshot_download
description:
Confirm a collection snapshot exists and return where to fetch it from — this tool does not transfer the (potentially huge) snapshot file itself; download it yourself (e.g. `curl`) from the returned `url`.

Example: {"collection_name": "docs", "snapshot_name": "docs-....snapshot"}

name: qdrant_storage_snapshot_create
description:
Create a snapshot of the whole storage: a snapshot of every collection plus the alias mapping (verified: no server configuration is included), not just one collection.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_storage_snapshot_list
description:
List the full-storage snapshots stored on the server.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_storage_snapshot_delete
description:
Delete a full-storage snapshot, freeing its disk space. Fails if the snapshot doesn't exist.

Example: {"snapshot_name": "full-....snapshot"}

name: qdrant_storage_snapshot_download
qdrant_telemetry
description:
Server-wide telemetry: build info, the number of collections and request counters by default; pass `details_level` 1 or more for per-collection stats, memory and hardware usage (verified: they are null at the default level). Not tied to any one collection.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_metrics_prometheus
description:
Return the URL where Qdrant serves Prometheus-format metrics — this tool does not fetch the metrics themselves (they're plain text, not JSON); point your Prometheus scraper at the returned `url` instead.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_quotas_get
description:
Current server-wide resource quotas (memory/disk limits) and actual usage.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_quotas_set
description:
Replace the server-wide resource quotas. The whole config is replaced, not merged (verified): every field you omit is reset — limits become unset and `enabled` becomes false. Read the current values with `qdrant_quotas_get` and pass every field you want to keep.

Example: {"enabled": true, "max_resident_memory_percent": 90}

name: qdrant_issues_list
description:
List the issues Qdrant has detected about its own configuration (e.g. a heavily-filtered field with no payload index). **API Beta** in Qdrant itself — the exact shape can change without notice, so this is returned as-is rather than forced into a fixed schema.

Example: {}

name: qdrant_issues_clear
description:
Clear all accumulated issues.

Example: {}
